cohort: 6,221 term infants born in Juan Ramon Jimenez Hospital during the years 2018 and 2019
finding: The main risk factors associated with foetal macrosomia were gestational age, male gender, multiparity, and pre-gestational diabetes, and macrosomia was associated with increased risk of caesarean section, shoulder dystocia, clavicle fracture, and brachial plexus palsy.
mod_finding: The risk of caesarean section in macrosomia is higher (OR 1.62, 95% CI; 1.3-2.1, p < 0.0001).
